answer: When k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated pattern, the protocol aggregates pairwise evidence and imposes penalties proportional to k(k−1)/2, or O(k²), rather than treating each signer in isolation. Detection also applies an exponential swarm-size multiplier to escrow forfeiture, so dividing stake among sybils cannot dilute the loss; asymmetric depreciation further reduces the value of recovered capital. “Lantern,” “oasis,” and “fable” may label identities, but do not exempt them from correlated-evidence analysis.
